overview: Constitution - evolution, features, Preamble, FR, FD, DPSP, amendments, significant provisions, basic structure: 41 official questions (2008-2024), 14 in 2019 alone and 9 in 2024. FR (9), evolution (6) and amendments (6) lead. Since 2019 the format is mostly statement-based (11) and 'choose the wrong answer' (8) with case-law reasoning (Kesavananda, Minerva, Coelho), not plain article numbers.

possibility.angle: Evolution: British Acts and the Constituent Assembly
possibility.what_they_ask: year of an Act or court; which Act gave dyarchy; CA committee chairmen; plan that composed the CA; who first proposed it

possibility.angle: Features and sources; federal vs unitary
possibility.what_they_ask: borrowed features by country; which feature is not federal; components of secularism
exact wording (liberty of thought ... worship); enacted last; justiciability; meaning of Republic, democratic, fraternity
citizen-only vs all-person rights; article pairs (21A, 24); habeas corpus scope; prisoners' rights; Ninth Schedule; Art. 14 concepts
which listed item is an FD (vs DPSP); citizens only; committees (Swaran Singh, Verma)
article number (Art. 40 panchayats); DPSP vs FR relation; order of DPSP amendments; Art. 31C cases
what a numbered amendment did; Bill number vs Act number; Art. 368 procedure; overriding judgments
modes of citizenship; Art. 370; Union vs Territory of India; Art. 300A
source (judge-made, Kesavananda 1973), who decides, what Parliament can amend, which case named which element

traps.trap: [Neighbour article] Article number shifted by one
traps.fix: Art. 40 panchayats; 41 work/assistance; 42 maternity; 23 forced labour; 24 child labour
traps.pyq: Village panchayats → Article 40 [group1-prelims-2008#34]; education and child labour → 21A and 24 [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#47]

traps.spot: List of articles 'denied to aliens' containing 23/24 or 20/21
traps.fix: Citizen-only: 15, 16, 19, 29, 30; all others available to every person
traps.pyq: Arts 23 and 24 excluded → 'I, II and IV only' [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#44]

traps.spot: 'Habeas corpus lies only against the executive'
traps.fix: Habeas corpus lies against State and private persons; mandamus does not lie against private persons
traps.pyq: Statement on executive-only is the wrong one [group1-prelims-2019-paper1#37]

traps.trap: DPSP item placed among Fundamental Duties
traps.spot: FD list with 'protect weaker sections from social injustice'
traps.fix: That is the State's duty under Art. 46 (DPSP); FD (51A) are citizens' duties
traps.pyq: Item I excluded → 'II, III and IV' [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#41]

traps.trap: Judge-made doctrine credited to Parliament or the 1950 text
traps.spot: 'Basic structure incorporated by an Act' / 'explained in the Constitution of 1950' / 'Parliament is supreme authority'
traps.fix: Kesavananda 1973 created it; courts decide its content; Parliament can amend any part without destroying it
traps.pyq: Statement I false [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#53]; correct option 'cannot be amended under Art. 368' [group1-prelims-2019-paper1#32]

traps.trap: Unitary feature slipped into federal list
traps.spot: 'Which is not a federal feature' with Governor
traps.fix: Centre-appointed Governor, single citizenship, emergencies are unitary

traps.spot: Art. 368 statements with 'prior permission of the President' or States initiating
traps.fix: Either House, minister or private member, no prior sanction; States cannot initiate; Art. 368 has two methods
The Preamble was adopted last to conform to the text; it is non-justiciable
traps.pyq: Statement on Preamble enacted first is false [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#45]

techniques.name: Who / where test for rights
techniques.how: [Citizen or person?] For each right ask: citizens only or all persons? against State only or private persons too?
techniques.example: Arts 29-30, 19, 16 citizen-only; 23-24 for all → 'I, II and IV only' [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#44]

techniques.name: Case-anchor timeline
techniques.how: Fix the landmark chain: Champakam 1951 - Golaknath 1967 - Kesavananda 1973 - Minerva 1980 - Coelho 2007; any statement giving a doctrine to the wrong case or date fails.
techniques.example: FD added 1976 cannot have been used in Kesavananda 1973 → statement III false [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#49]

techniques.name: Bill number is not Act number
techniques.how: When an option set mixes 100+ numbers, check if the stem says 'Bill' or 'Act'.
techniques.example: EWS: 124th Bill = 103rd Act → '124th Constitutional Amendment Bill' [group1-prelims-2019-paper2#108]

techniques.name: Exact-wording recall
techniques.how: For Preamble wording questions, recite the clause in full; options that drop one word fall.
techniques.example: Liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship → only the five-word option survives [group1-prelims-2019-paper1#52]

techniques.name: Plan-stage sorting
techniques.how: For CA history sort: proposed (Roy 1934, INC 1935) - offered (Cripps 1942) - composed (Cabinet Mission 1946) - sovereign (Independence Act 1947).
techniques.example: 'composed roughly on the lines suggested by' → Cabinet Mission [group1-prelims-2017-paper1#143]; first idea → M.N. Roy [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#27]

confusions.remember: traffic and forced labour vs child labour below 14 in hazardous work
education 6-14 as FR vs early childhood care below 6 (DPSP)
State protects weaker sections vs citizens' duties
British (negative) vs American (positive); both in Art. 14
States only vs States + UTs + acquired territories
against State and private vs public authorities only
created basic structure, struck 31C 2nd part vs limited amending power and FR-DPSP harmony
dyarchy in provinces vs provincial autonomy, dyarchy at Centre proposed
offer rejected vs actually composed the CA
Rules, Steering, Finance and Staff vs Advisory (FR, minorities), Provincial Constitution
Sikkim associate State vs full State
recommended FD vs identified legal provisions to enforce some
suits and contracts of Government vs right to property

anchors: Regulating Act 1773 → Supreme Court at Calcutta 1774; Pitt's India Act 1784
Constituent Assembly per Cabinet Mission 1946; first idea M.N. Roy 1934
Art. 21A by 86th Amendment 2002; RTE Act in force 1 April 2010
Kesavananda Bharati 1973 = basic structure; Minerva Mills 1980; I.R. Coelho 2007 (Ninth Schedule after 24 April 1973)
FD: 42nd Amendment 1976 (Swaran Singh), 11th duty by 86th 2002; citizens only
Citizenship modes: birth, descent, registration, naturalisation, incorporation
checklist: Negative stem ('wrong answer', 'except')? Mark it before reading.
Article number options adjacent? Recall the exact article content.
Rights question: citizen or person? State or private?
Doctrine statements: which case, which year, judge-made or enacted?
Amendment chronology: order by amendment number.
Bill or Act number? Read the stem word.
